title: Background agent brief
description: What a background agent is given. Every field exists to remove latitude the agent would otherwise use to make a red result look green.

working_directory.description: The one directory this agent owns. Name any directory another agent owns under `do_not_touch`.

commands.description: Run these verbatim, in order. Do not adapt them. If one cannot run, mark it blocked and continue to the next.

forbidden.description: Name the workarounds you can foresee, not just 'be careful'. e.g. no --release, no git stash, no substituting a different version of a pinned dependency, no editing to make a test pass.

counts_as_a_finding.description: Outcomes that must be reported rather than treated as success. e.g. a suite that skipped for a missing dependency is a finding, not a pass.

report_path.description: Where to write the report, valid against agent-report.schema.json.

long_running.description: If true: wait in a bounded poll loop inside one long-timeout call. Nothing will wake you - ending your turn early abandons the job.

requires.description: Preconditions, checked BEFORE running anything - the requirements channel. An unmet requirement makes the job `could_not` without the agent ever having to decide mid-run whether a workaround is acceptable. Declaring them up front is what removes that discretion.

what.description: e.g. 'sqlite3 pinned at 3.50.4', 'network access to sqlite.org'

check.description: A command that exits 0 when the requirement is met.

if_unmet.description: Always report and stop. Never substitute. Named here so the tempting substitution is visibly ruled out.
